request: Add a magnitude filter to the earthquakes API so the map can hide small quakes.
us: As a map operator monitoring seismic activity, I want to request earthquakes above a minimum magnitude from /api/earthquakes, so I can focus the view on significant events and cut noise.
context_query: earthquake seismic magnitude data API route USGS
acs: GET /api/earthquakes?minMagnitude=5 returns only earthquakes whose magnitude is >= 5.
When minMagnitude is absent, the response is unchanged: every earthquake is returned.
When minMagnitude is invalid (non-numeric, empty, or negative) the route must NOT return 500; it returns the full unfiltered set.
The response 'total' field equals the number of earthquakes actually returned after filtering.
The existing Cache-Control response header is preserved unchanged.

request: The /api/health endpoint list is stale and hardcoded. Make it reflect the real API routes.
us: As an operator, I want /api/health to report the actual set of API routes the app exposes, so the status payload never drifts from the real surface as routes are added or removed.
context_query: health status endpoint api routes list operational
acs: The 'endpoints' array is derived at runtime from the filesystem (scanning the src/app/api route tree), not a hardcoded literal list.
The returned list includes routes currently missing from the hardcoded version, e.g. /api/cctv and /api/osint/phone.
Nested routes appear with their full path (e.g. /api/osint/phone, not just /api/osint).
The route returns HTTP 200 and never throws, even if the directory scan fails (it falls back gracefully).
Each listed endpoint is a string path beginning with /api/.

request: The space-weather route hits NOAA on every request. Add a short server-side cache to cut upstream calls.
us: As a backend owner, I want /api/space-weather to serve a recently-cached payload instead of refetching NOAA on every request, so we reduce upstream load and latency without serving stale data for long.
context_query: space weather NOAA solar Kp index fetch route caching
acs: An in-memory cache holds the computed payload with a bounded TTL (on the order of 30-120 seconds).
Within the TTL window, a second request returns the cached payload WITHOUT issuing new NOAA fetch calls.
After the TTL expires, the route refetches from NOAA and refreshes the cache.
A Cache-Control response header is added consistent with the TTL.
On upstream failure the route still responds without throwing (existing resilience preserved).

request: Let the live-news API be filtered by country and category from the query string.
us: As a frontend consuming /api/live-news, I want to request feeds filtered by country and/or category, so I can show a region- or topic-specific subset without filtering client-side.
context_query: live news feeds channels country category broadcast
acs: GET /api/live-news?country=US returns only feeds whose country is US.
GET /api/live-news?category=finance returns only feeds whose category is finance.
country and category can be combined and are applied together (AND).
Filtering is case-insensitive for the provided values.
The response 'total' equals the number of feeds returned after filtering; with no params the full list is returned unchanged.

request: Add an optional result limit to the earthquakes API so the client can cap how many it loads.
us: As a client rendering earthquake markers, I want to cap the number of events returned by /api/earthquakes via a limit parameter, so large swarms don't overload the map.
context_query: earthquake seismic events API route limit results
acs: GET /api/earthquakes?limit=10 returns at most 10 earthquakes.
Results are capped by taking the strongest (highest magnitude) events first when the limit is applied.
When limit is absent or invalid (non-numeric, <= 0), all earthquakes are returned.
The 'total' field equals the number of earthquakes actually returned after the limit is applied.
The existing Cache-Control response header is preserved unchanged.
